newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmens promised cheap flour after poor harvest.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens promised cheap flour after poor harvest.

text.p: Turkmens, hit by food shortages following a disastrous grain harvest in the former Soviet republic, have been promised a monthly ration of subsidised flour, an agriculture ministry official said on Tuesday.
People in the countryside will be able to buy eight kg of flour at a nominal 25 manats per kg under the new scheme, the official told Reuters.
Those living in the capital are entitled to six kg.
President Saparmurat Niyazov was quoted by official media saying the subsidies aimed at "social fairness".
Prices for subsidised bread, obtained by the 3.8 million population only with ration cards outside Ashgabat, doubled in December.
Those who once poured into the capital from the countryside to buy up scarce loaves slowed to a trickle after transport costs rose nine times in the same month.
Niyazov, the republic's former Communist party boss, is intent on making the largely desert nation self-sufficient in grains with Soviet-style production plans.

But the 1996 grain harvest was a meagre 400,000 tonnes, according to official figures, well below 1995's one million-tonne crop, while a shortage of feed grains saw 20 percent of the Turkmenistan's livestock die last year.
